title: Adding and Subtracting in Scientific Notation

steps.body: Adding and subtracting are DIFFERENT from multiplying and dividing: you can't just combine exponents. Like fractions needing a common denominator, scientific notation needs matching exponents before you add or subtract the coefficients.
Rewrite the smaller term using the same power of 10 before combining coefficients.

widget.prompt: Rewrite 3 × 10³ as 0.3 × 10⁴. Explore the place shift, then enter the shared value of both forms.

numericErrors.feedback: That treats 0.3 as 3. Multiplying 0.3 by 10⁴ gives 3,000, not 30,000.
That shifts only three places. The form 0.3 × 10⁴ equals 3,000.

widget.explorationFeedback: Inspect the coefficient and all four place shifts before checking.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Move the decimal in 0.3 four places to the right: 0.3 × 10⁴ = 3,000.

predict.prompt: Before adding scientific-notation numbers, what must be true of their powers of 10?

options.label: The coefficients can combine without rewriting

predict.reveal: Addition combines like place-value units. Rewrite both terms with the same power of 10, then add their coefficients; adding exponents is a multiplication rule.

steps.body: The same rule applies to subtraction: convert to matching exponents first. (5×10⁶) − (2×10⁵): rewrite 2×10⁵ as 0.2×10⁶, then subtract: 5 − 0.2 = 4.8, giving 4.8 × 10⁶.

explanationVariants: Converting to the bigger exponent (5) first, then subtracting coefficients.

commonBuilds.feedback: That subtracts the coefficients directly without matching exponents — rewrite 4×10⁴ as 0.4×10⁵ first.
The matched exponent should be the BIGGER one, 5, not 4.
That subtracts the exponents like dividing — subtraction doesn't combine exponents that way.

explanationVariants: When exponents already match, just add the coefficients directly: 3+4=7, giving 7×10⁵.

That's not how matching exponents work here — since both already share exponent 5, just add 3+4=7: 7×10⁵.

widget.successFeedback: Right — same exponent, so just add coefficients: 3+4=7.

explanationVariants: Same exponent (7), so just subtract coefficients: 9−4=5, giving 5×10⁷.

That's the right value before renormalizing, but 14 isn't a valid coefficient — and it's easier to just match exponents to 7 first: 1.4×10⁷.

steps.body: Match exponents FIRST, then add or subtract the coefficients directly.
takeaways: Unlike multiply/divide, exponents don't combine when adding or subtracting.
Convert to a shared exponent (usually the larger one) before combining coefficients.
Once exponents match, just add or subtract the coefficients.
